questions.q: What is a query execution plan?
options: The database engine's chosen strategy for actually running a specific query
A written report the admin files after a slow query occurs
A fixed setting that never changes no matter what the query looks like
A list of every user who ran the same query that day
questions.explain: The execution plan is the concrete strategy the database chooses, given the table, conditions, and available indexes.

questions.q: What happens during a full table scan?
options: The database checks every single row in the table, one at a time, because no useful index exists
The database deletes rows that don't match the query
The database automatically builds an index before running the query
The query is rejected outright
questions.explain: With no useful index, the database has no shortcut and falls back to evaluating every row individually.

questions.q: Why does a full table scan matter so much more on a large table than a small one?
options: Checking every row scales with the table's size, so the gap between scanning and an indexed lookup grows as the table grows
Full table scans only exist on tables above one million rows
Small tables never support indexes at all
Table size has no real effect on query speed
questions.explain: On a small table a scan is barely noticeable; on a table with hundreds of thousands of rows, the gap between scanning everything and jumping to matches becomes very real.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is a common real root cause of a slow query against a large table?
options: A full table scan happening because the filtered field isn't covered by any existing index
The instance running out of available licenses
The user's browser cache being full
The report having too many columns displayed
questions.explain: A full scan on a large table, caused by a missing covering index, is one of the most common real explanations for a slow query.

questions.q: What is the practical fix for converting a slow full-scan query into a fast one?
options: Add or confirm an index that actually covers the fields the query filters or sorts on
Rewrite the report to display fewer rows per page
Ask every user to run the report less often
Disable the Slow Request Log so the query no longer gets flagged
questions.explain: The right index gives the database a shortcut, so it picks an indexed-lookup plan instead of falling back to a full scan.
